Hi Priya / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture. If I missed anything, please flag.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Intermittent latency spikes during peak trading hours (US market open) causing timeouts on inference calls
- High per-token cost at current scale (approx ~1.8–2.2M tokens/day)
- Need for predictable throughput for batch scoring and online requests, and an on-prem option for regulated workloads

Goals we captured:
- Latency SLOs: p50 target <= 150ms, p95 target <= 600ms for single-turn text-gen endpoints
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/s for online scoring, burstable to 350 req/s for limited windows; daily token volume ~2M
- Model support: ability to run a mix of LLM variants (fine-tuned Llama2-13B class + larger 70B for complex responses) with quantized variants for cost control
- Deployment: prefer dedicated GPU pool in us-west with automated fallbacks to hosted nodes in another region for resilience

What Redwood will deliver next (actions):
1) Rishi to share a preliminary capacity / cost calc and recommended GPU instance types (A100/H100) + quantization strategy — by EOD today.
2) I'll send the draft SLO worksheet and a proposed deployment topology diagram (attached).
3) Align on compliance requirements and on-prem packaging details (Priya to share internal checklist).
4) Schedule a deployment design review next week to finalize topology and failover policy.

Attachments: 2026-03-04_slo_requirements.xlsx, 2026-03-04_deployment_topology_diagram.png

Thanks Marissa — attaching the capacity calc and a few notes from the technical side. High-level thoughts below.

Short answers up-front:
- Recommended GPUs: H100 for 70B inference in production (best perf/cost at scale) or A100-80GB for heavy quantized 70B workloads; 40GB A100 can be used for 13B quantized variants.
- Quantization: GGUF 4-bit for 13B gives ~2.5–3x speedups and ~4x memory reduction; 70B will need 8-bit or 4-bit with model-specific validation.
- Batching & latency tradeoffs: to hit p50 <=150ms at 120 req/s we should target small dynamic batching (batch sizes 1–8) with prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts; p95 budget will depend on tail behavior — I modeled p95 ~ 450–700ms depending on batching and async queue depth.

Notes from capacity calc (attached: 2026-03-04_capacity_calc.csv):
- For 120 sustained rps of short prompts (avg 60 tokens), H100 nodes (N per node) -> estimate 6 H100s to keep p95 under 600ms with redundancy 2x for failover.
- If we prioritize cost and accept slightly higher tail latencies, a mixed pool (A100 for quantized 13B + H100 for 70B heavy queries) reduces monthly infra by ~28% in our model.
- Autoscaling: configured to scale based on queue size + token/sec; warm pool to avoid cold-start latency for critical windows.

Suggested topology (see diagram):
- Primary: Dedicated us-west cluster (private VPC) serving online traffic with pinned model versions and GPUs.
- Secondary: Hosted regional fallback in us-east for failover and longer-running batch jobs.
- Compliance/on-prem: we can package an appliance bundle with private control plane and local KMS integration — will need their security checklist to size networking and audit-log retention.

I've attached the calc and diagram. Happy to walk through numbers on the design call.

Attachments: 2026-03-04_capacity_calc.csv
